subject: Azure private offer: escrowed commitment structure & quarterly true-up
messages:
From: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@stratussystems.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@stratussystems.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 09:42:00 +0000
Subject: Initial ask - Azure marketplace private offer: multi-year escrow + quarterly true-up

Hi Lauren,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Stratus is interested in moving forward with a private offer on Azure but we need to align the commercial structure before procurement can issue an LOI. A couple of requirements from legal/procurement:

- We'd like the commitment to be escrowed (funds held in marketplace escrow) for the first 12 months to satisfy our internal spend controls.
- The deal will be a 2-year commitment, but we need quarterly true-ups so we can smooth consumption across BU forecasts.
- Can you provide a pricing matrix that maps annual prepay tiers to quarterly release cadence and sponsor credits for overages?
- We also need a cancellation / unwind schedule for year-2 in case of divestiture.

If you can share a draft private-offer term sheet and an example payment cadence (PO -> escrow -> release to Redwood by quarter), I can take it to procurement next week.

Appreciate any examples you can share — we have a target internal approval by mid-December.

Best,
Alex
Alex Mercer
Sr. Procurement Manager
Stratus Systems

P.S. attaching our standard procurement questionnaire (see referenced attachment in procurement inbox).

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@stratussystems.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 11:07:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Initial ask - Azure marketplace private offer: multi-year escrow + quarterly true-up

Hi Alex — thanks for the clear list. Attaching a first-pass pricing_matrix_v2.xlsx and a private-offer term summary (redwood_private_offer_terms.pdf). Quick notes below, then a few questions so we align the draft: 

- Proposed structure (high level): 2-year commitment with an annual prepay per marketplace contract. Year 1 funds are placed into Azure marketplace escrow on receipt of the PO; releases to Redwood are scheduled at the start of each quarter (Q1 release = 25% of year1 prepay, etc.). Year 2 can be pre-funded at signing or invoiced with an upfront 30-day net.
- Discounting: blended discount tiers by ARR band: 12% for >= $750k/yr, 8% for $350-749k, 4% for < $350k. We applied an additional 150bp sponsor credit for customers committing to escrowed annual prepay (reflects lower unit cost/booking certainty).
- Quarterly true-up: we propose a lookback true-up at the end of each quarter. If consumption exceeds released credits, overages will draw against the next quarter release; if consumption is under, unused credits roll forward within the 12-month escrow window. True-ups settle in marketplace credits (preferred) or invoice depending on your treasury requirements.
- Cancellation/unwind: standard early termination schedule: 90-day notice, pro-rata refund on unused escrowed funds minus a 5% administrative fee; if the unwind is due to change-in-control/divestiture, we include a capped transfer provision (requires prior Redwood approval).

Questions for you:
1) Would Stratus prefer year-2 to be pre-funded into escrow as well, or left as an invoiced commitment with an annual PO?
2) For sponsor credit application — should it be applied to per-token rates or to reserved throughput capacity (e.g., dedicated pool credit)?
3) Any compliance paperwork (SOC2 artifacts, data residency) we should attach directly to the offer package?

I've looped Marissa to confirm the marketplace private-offer mechanics (DocuSign + Azure escrow flow) and Rishi to confirm the sponsor-credit accounting treatment. If it helps, we can do a 30-min alignment with procurement tomorrow afternoon.

—Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Head of Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: pricing_matrix_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet), redwood_private_offer_terms.pdf (summary)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 08:22:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Initial ask - Azure marketplace private offer: multi-year escrow + quarterly true-up

Alex — quick operational clarifications from marketplace side: 

- Azure Marketplace supports escrow releases by schedule; we will propose a quarterly release cadence tied to an agreed usage band. If Stratus wants year-2 pre-funded, Azure will hold both years in escrow and we can define a release schedule across 8 quarters (same release rules apply).
- DocuSign flow: we will include an appendix that maps PO numbers to escrow buckets. That appendix is what the marketplace uses to authorize releases; please confirm the PO numbering convention you will use.
- Billing/true-up options: if you prefer credit settlement (recommended), overages are deducted from the next scheduled release. If you opt for invoiced true-ups, Redwood will issue a marketplace invoice at quarter close and Stratus pays the difference within net-30. 

Operational ask: can you share an example PO naming convention and whether treasury requires physical remittance (wire) vs. marketplace card? That determines whether Azure requires an additional transfer SLA.

I will prepare a short appendix for the private-offer that codifies the quarterly release rules and the unwind workflow for year-2. Will send that by Monday EOD.

—Marissa
Sr. Deals Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@stratussystems.com>

Subject: Re: Initial ask - Azure marketplace private offer: multi-year escrow + quarterly true-up

Thanks all — this is helpful. A few final confirmations from procurement side: 

- Stratus will pre-fund Year 1 into Azure marketplace escrow. For Year 2, procurement requests the option to pre-fund at signing OR issue an annual PO at the start of Y2 (we will confirm by LOI).
- PO naming convention: STRAT-2027-REDWOOD-<BU>-<PO#>. Treasury will use wire for initial remittance; confirm if Azure requires any additional documentation for a wire into escrow.
- Sponsor credit: we prefer the sponsor credit to apply against reserved throughput capacity (helps us normalize unit costs for BU chargebacks).
- Cancellation: procurement accepts the proposed 5% administrative fee on refund; please include the transfer provision language in the appendix for review.

Next step — procurement will prepare an LOI with the above points and target signature by 2026-12-15. Can we schedule a 30-min call on Wed 12/2 to align the DocuSign + Azure escrow appendix?

Best,
Alex
Sr. Procurement Manager
Stratus Systems
